events.title: Birth of Alexander Graham Bell
events.description: Alexander Graham Bell was born in Edinburgh, Scotland. He became a scientist, inventor, and teacher of the deaf, and was awarded the first U.S. patent for the telephone in 1876.
events.significance: Bell's invention of the telephone transformed global communication and laid the groundwork for modern telecommunications.

events.title: Tsar Alexander II Emancipates the Serfs
events.description: Tsar Alexander II signed the Emancipation Manifesto (March 3 in the New Style calendar; February 19 in the Old Style), freeing millions of serfs in the Russian Empire from bondage to landowners.
events.significance: It was among the most sweeping social reforms in Russian history, reshaping the country's economy and society and weakening the old feudal order.

events.title: The Star-Spangled Banner Becomes the U.S. National Anthem
events.description: President Herbert Hoover signed a congressional act officially designating 'The Star-Spangled Banner' as the national anthem of the United States. The lyrics came from Francis Scott Key's 1814 poem written during the War of 1812.
events.significance: The act formalized a long-standing patriotic song as a lasting national symbol of the United States.

events.title: Rodney King Beating in Los Angeles
events.description: Los Angeles police officers severely beat Rodney King after a traffic stop, and the incident was recorded on videotape by a bystander and broadcast widely.
events.significance: The acquittal of the officers in 1992 sparked the Los Angeles riots and intensified national debate over police brutality and racial inequality in America.

events.title: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk Signed
events.description: Soviet Russia and the Central Powers signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, ending Russia's participation in World War I. Russia ceded large territories including Poland, the Baltic states, and Ukraine.
events.significance: The treaty allowed the Bolsheviks to consolidate power at home, though it was annulled after Germany's defeat later in 1918.
